items.title: Britain's new PM is redefining populist anger
items.description: Britain's new left-leaning PM Andy Burnham has seized the same public discontent driving Nigel Farage on the populist right but with a very different agenda. As One Nation climbs in the polls, Australia should be paying attention.

items.title: Inside this street food market are signs of a crashing currency
items.description: Indonesia's rupiah has fallen to historic lows against the US dollar, causing damage "in most of the economy", analysts say.

items.title: Trump is not shy of collecting spoils, and the US presidency has plenty
items.description: The US president's most-recent filings indicate he pocketed more than $US2.2 billion last year through ventures ostensibly run by his family.

items.title: Greens draw betting perk line ahead of gambling showdown
items.description: The Greens are not prepared to vote on the government's gambling legislation, outlining some of their main concerns around "predatory" behaviour.

items.title: Survivors uncover new evidence in Australia’s contaminated blood scandal
items.description: The 1980s contaminated blood crisis devastated the lives of thousands of Australians who were infected with hepatitis C or HIV. Now, survivor Tristan Stanley, who contracted hep C as a child, has uncovered government documents that raise troubling questions about the scandal.

items.title: Planes in tarmac near miss at Sydney Airport
items.description: A cabin crew member is injured when Jetstar and Qatar Airlines planes almost collide on the tarmac at Sydney Airport.

items.title: 'Very debilitating': Hunter Biden opens up about his father's cancer
items.description: Former US president Joe Biden's prostate cancer has spread to other parts of his body and is causing him pain, even as he continues to speak out on public issues, according to his son Hunter.

items.title: Infantino denies 'defamatory' affair claims made in British newspaper
items.description: FIFA boss Gianna Infantino dismisses allegations of an affair while working at UEFA as 'categorically untrue'.

items.title: Wildfire forces more than 20,000 people evacuate homes in western Canada
items.description: Thousands of people in British Columbia have been ordered to flee a fast-moving wildfire that nearly doubled in size overnight.

items.title: Live: Miller turns goalkicking hero with Suns and Giants in epic arm-wrestle
items.description: Gold Coast finds an unlikely source of goals in the form of veteran midfielder Touk Miller as it takes a lead into the final quarter against GWS. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Raiders season on the line in topsy-turvy, high-scoring shoot out
items.description: The Newcastle Knights will look to keep their slim hopes of a top four finish alive when they head to Canberra to take on the Raiders. Follow live.

items.title: Army of volunteers races to save one of Australia's rarest orchids
items.description: It takes years of work, dozens of volunteers, picky pollinators and a special fungus to save Australia’s endangered orchids. Here's why people drive from all over the country to do it anyway.

items.title: Bird flu is spreading across Australia — this is what you need to know
items.description: There are more than 200 confirmed cases of the deadly H5N1 bird flu strain across Australia. Here's how it spreads and what to know.

items.title: Australia's 999th Wallaby on his injury-riddled road to Test debut
items.description: Isaac Henry will run the prospect of fresh ink past his wife but is otherwise assured he can make a permanent Wallabies mark after a hard-earned debut in Osaka.

items.title: Love story: The grief and relief that comes with the death of your 'big love'
items.description: Hilda Quiroga says she was "struck" by Steve Mayer from the moment they first met until his death at 53 through voluntary assisted dying.

items.title: White chocolate tart with burnt honey and thyme
items.description: This decadent tart has a chocolate and hazelnut crust, no-bake white chocolate and cream cheese filling and is ready in only 30 minutes.

items.title: Do you believe in life after love? What about music quizzes?
items.description: Can you feel something inside you say 'Try your hand at the Spicks and Specks quiz'? Well, you've come to the right place.

items.title: Parents urged to restrict cow's milk for toddlers
items.description: Paediatricians across Australia are concerned about a jump in iron deficiency in young children due to too much cow's milk, and the need to better educate parents about the issue.

items.title: Here are the questions asked in Australia's first complete census
items.description: When you sit down to fill in the census, you will be taking part in an ancient human tradition.

items.title: Armed officers to bolster security at Melbourne hospitals under opposition proposal

items.title: New attempt to revive smelter conditional on environmental concession
items.description: The union representing workers at Australia's last manganese smelter says there are parties interested in taking over the site, days after the business was placed in liquidation.

items.title: Australian Beacroft smashes U20 world record to continue golden form
items.description: Australian race walker Isaac Beacroft smashes the U20 5km record to add to his Commonwealth Games gold.

items.title: Regional general store closing after larger competitors arrive
items.description: After 102 years, the South West's historic Vasse General Store is closing its doors amid staunch retail competition in the growing residential area.

items.title: How Ukraine is striking Russia where it hurts most
items.description: Ukraine's 40-day campaign to take the war to the heart of Russia increases the strain on Russian businesses, people and air defences, analysts say.

items.title: After a big defeat, US pro-Israel lobby sets sights on midterms
items.description: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee lobby group boasts of its track record of success deciding election winners as it endorses candidates that support its cause.
